$comment: Which hosted CI checks BLOCK a release, and which are informational. PRD R2.
Defined once, here, so the release gate and GitHub branch protection cannot
disagree. scanner/test/release-check.test.js asserts every name observed on a
commit appears in one of the two lists, so a newly added job cannot silently
become un-tiered.
WHY THE SPLIT EXISTS. remote-ci-green previously required EVERY check on the
commit. On 2026-08-09 a publish was blocked for 15+ minutes by realworld-bench
while 8 of 9 checks were green. That job measures detection rate against public
vulnerable apps — a quality TREND, not a statement about whether this build is
publishable. The same over-broad requirement is why routine pushes to main have
been reporting 'Bypassed rule violations': protection demanded checks that are
not correctness gates, so the bypass became habitual, and a rule that is
habitually bypassed is not a control.
BLOCKING means: red or pending here stops the release. Correctness.
INFORMATIONAL means: still runs, still reported, and a FAILING one prints a loud
warning at publish time — but it does not gate. Trend regressions must stay
visible; the point is that they are not release blockers, not that they are
ignorable.
Adding a job? Put it in a list deliberately. The default is blocking, because a
check nobody classified is a check nobody thought about.
THESE ARE CHECK-RUN NAMES (jobs), NOT WORKFLOW NAMES. The first draft of this
file listed 'ci' and 'codeql', which are workflow names and never appear as
check runs — they would have matched nothing here, and if branch protection had
been configured from this list, pull requests would have hung forever waiting on
contexts that never report. The names below were read from
`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/main/check-runs`. Verify the same way before
adding one.
SELF means: this check run IS the job the release gate is executing inside.
The release workflow's publish job runs the gate, so the gate observes a check
named 'publish' that is in_progress — itself — and waits for it to finish. It
never can. Every tag push therefore failed the gate on a self-reference while
all nine real checks were green, and both v0.135.0 and v0.136.0 failed this way
before it was diagnosed. A self check is EXCLUDED, not trusted: it says nothing
about the commit, so treating it as informational would be wrong for the same
reason treating it as blocking is.

vscode-extension (added 0.141.0) is BLOCKING. It builds the shipped VS Code extension and asserts the built bundle carries the current scanner-resolution logic. The extension spent every release unable to find the scanner at all — a hardcoded cache-path version that no install creates — so this is a correctness gate, not a trend.

nvim-plugin (0.142.0) is BLOCKING and jetbrains-plugin is INFORMATIONAL, and the split is the point. Loading a lua plugin headlessly costs seconds and fails only when the plugin is actually broken. Building the JetBrains plugin downloads a full IntelliJ distribution, so a red result there is far more often the network or a JetBrains release than a statement about this code — and a gate that is habitually red stops being read, which is the lesson realworld-bench already taught. The correctness half of the JetBrains surface (plugin.xml's factoryClass resolves to the Kotlin class it names) is asserted offline and blocking in test/ide-surfaces.test.js.
